  2. Kids and parents to cover

Two generations, one income, no margin for error

For kids and parents to cover — typically age 45–60.

This is the hardest stage to insure and the one where getting the details wrong is most expensive. Senior-parent cover in particular rewards precision.

What is actually at risk

Parents over 60 face co-pays, loading and full waiting periods

Premiums rise steeply, insurers add a co-payment share, and pre-existing conditions — which most people over 60 have — sit behind a 2 to 3 year wait. Which insurer you pick decides whether that wait is two years or three.

A senior couple costs ₹66,505–₹78,923/yr at ₹15 L cover

Your corporate floater will not take them

Most employer plans either exclude parents outright or price them as a punitive add-on with thin limits. And like all group cover, it ends the day you change jobs — taking your parents' only protection with it.

Your kids' education corpus is exposed

College costs are a fixed future liability sitting on a single income. Without term cover sized to it, that corpus is the first thing that gets liquidated.

You are the single point of failure for two generations

Parents above you, children below, and both financially dependent on you continuing to earn. That is the definition of a risk that has to be transferred rather than absorbed.
